HostPreimage.description: The reviewed three-way comparison for one host.apply effect. The executor owns one deterministic projection of that effect's exact native target scope, including target identity, absence, managed content and relevant metadata. Baseline, live and proposed use that same projection; their digests do not contain native values. The baseline is the state expected from the accepted source under the matching owner/resource precondition. A projection cannot omit a target that the effect may replace. This record does not observe native state, establish capture custody or authorize an effect by itself.

effect_step.description: Exactly one matching Plan.effects step, which supplies the executor, resource and input scope. Step action names cannot exempt an effect from comparison.

baseline_digest.description: Projection of the currently accepted managed state. A target without an accepted baseline is represented by explicit absence in the same projection, not by an invented successful observation.

live_digest.description: Projection actually observed when preparing this review, including administrator edits relative to the accepted baseline. Every disposition is limited to this exact live preimage.

proposed_digest.description: Projection that the exact reviewed source and effect would establish. Preserve requires this digest to equal live_digest; retaining different live state cannot be reported as applying the proposed state.

disposition.description: Explicit administrator disposition of the reviewed live state. Preserve keeps it and requires the proposed projection to match it. Capture permits replacement only after the executor verifies durable custody of that exact live preimage as a reviewable source proposal or recovery artifact. Overwrite permits replacing the reviewed live preimage without that capture requirement. None permits replacing a later edit, and capture neither publishes nor adopts a source proposal.

capture_digest.description: Exact retained capture artifact digest, required only for capture. The executor must independently verify that this artifact covers the effect scope and live_digest and remains in its custody before replacement. A digest supplied in a plan is not custody evidence.

input_digests.description: Complete immutable material required by the reviewed subject and effects, including every subject argument typed MaterialDigest and each effect input. Material is retained as exact owner content or protected owner records with their referenced closure before accepted work can depend on it. Merely naming a digest does not verify custody. Integrity-only schema hashes, comparison preimages and expected predecessors do not require invented material bytes.

source_digests.description: Accepted source identities checked as state preconditions. This list does not establish material custody. Any exact source snapshot or reconstruction material required by the subject or effects is also retained under input_digests; precondition hashes alone are insufficient.

resource.description: The exact resource changed by this effect under its executor. Each executor/resource pair must have a corresponding plan precondition; multiple changed resources require separate effect entries.

summary.description: Explain this specific effect in administrator language. The executor, resource and input digest define its scope; this text is bound by the plan digest.

host_preimages.description: Required exactly for a host.apply subject and covers every effect step exactly once, including delegated effects and arbitrary executor action names. The plan digest binds every comparison and disposition. Before each native effect, its executor must reobserve the same projection, reject any mismatch with the reviewed live_digest, and maintain exclusion or an equivalent compare-and-apply guarantee through mutation. Earlier offline validation cannot supply that native guarantee.

checkpoint_required.description: Whether execution requires the plan-specific recovery checkpoint. A checkpoint requirement is not evidence that a checkpoint exists or has passed a restore drill.

interruption.description: Expected disruption to the named resources and their dependants, including planned downtime. A client disconnect alone does not stop work already accepted by a local owner.

recovery.description: Candidate recovery procedures for this exact plan. This list neither executes recovery nor guarantees automatic undo. none-needed is exclusive.

blockers.description: Known reasons this proposal cannot currently be admitted. A blocked plan remains available for inspection and explanation.

summary.description: The intended outcome in administrator language, naming the application, host or other resource affected. It describes a proposed change, not a completed result.

data_consequences.description: Explain which persistent data is preserved, modified, replaced or removed, including possible loss of writes after a selected recovery point. State when normal application writes may resume; do not promise preservation merely because execution can be retried.

recovery_limits.description: Explain what can be resumed or restored after interruption and what requires another explicit decision. Name irreversible effects or first-write limits where applicable. Cancellation and returning to an earlier software release do not imply that data is rolled back.

Plan.description: A reviewable proposal for exact owner-authorized work. Human consequences, exact effect targets and host.apply live-change dispositions are part of its digest. Preparing, reviewing or publishing this plan does not accept or execute it.

plan_digest.description: Digest of the exact retained reviewed Plan, including its original ID. Together with this owner it is the complete plan.get lookup, independently recoverable from this Operation without client state.

Operation.description: An exact request accepted by a local management program. Its execution state and effect certainty answer different questions; failed, cancelled or quarantined work can still retain effects and resource holds. Succeeded requires known effect certainty in every representation, including pages and transferred snapshots. The witness owner identity and epoch equal this owner; shared semantic validation enforces that join. Signature authentication, record-digest verification, current authority and native outcome verification remain independently required receiving boundaries. The exact retained Plan is identified by owner and plan_digest and remains readable despite admission expiry while this Operation requires accepted replay or recovery custody. The human caller can disconnect without erasing the accepted responsibility. The witness subject_digest is the digest of the complete canonical Operation object with only witness omitted; witness owner, state and generation equal the enclosing snapshot. Kind is acceptance only for accepted and effect for running, waiting and every terminal state; an effect witness may explicitly report uncertainty. These deterministic joins are required in every representation and do not authenticate the signing key or establish native truth. Schema and selected-adapter producer actions require a non-null committed result before succeeded. Native effect completion without that custody remains unresolved; terminal success is never an intermediate promise to attach output later. Independently installed recovery compatibility may admit an exact prior result schema with the same action-owned URI; complete payload verification against its pinned reader remains mandatory.

Observation.description: An observation of a named resource with explicit provenance and time. Operating intent, reachability, power, activity, health-check support, health, and data protection remain separate facts. An observation is never permission to change or delete the resource. A present witness must name this exact owner epoch; authentication and verification of what it attests remain independent receiving boundaries. A large observation may be delivered through an exact Observation RecordReference under the same protected resource, preserving every evidence digest and its original provenance and observation time.

origin.description: Evidence provenance. A cached observation retains its original observation time and values; reading it again does not make it current owner evidence.

reachability.description: Observed ability to contact the resource through its selected management path. Unreachable does not establish failed health, stopped activity, or a powered-off host.

power_state.description: Observed host power state, using independent evidence when the host cannot reply. Application and other non-host resources use not-applicable; an inactive application does not imply its host is off.

activity.description: Observed execution activity, separate from desired activity, host power, and health.

health_check.description: Whether a health check is supported for this resource. An unsupported or unknown check cannot supply a healthy or unhealthy result.

health.description: Reported result of a supported health check. Unknown preserves absence of evidence; sleep, disconnection, and missing check support are separate dimensions.

state.description: Local owner admission lifecycle with exact meanings and legal edges in states.json. It is derived from retained preparation, ordered advances (including native lifecycle decisions), and any explicit recovery abandonment; neither a client nor a transfer may relabel it. completed is equivalent to the installed terminal procedure phase; cancelled is terminal without claiming child termination or hold release.

generation.description: The receiving owner replica generation for this workflow capsule, incremented after every durable phase, driver or custody change. It is separate from participant resource generations and driver_term. workflow.advance and workflow.transfer compare this exact local value; replicas may have different generations.

Workflow.description: A finite procedure coordinating exact participant operations while each local owner retains authority and accepted state. A workflow is not a permanent central controller or an authorization supplied by an optional tracker. Each receiving owner retains its own identified, generation-checked capsule before child effects. Preparation records no accepted native operation. An authorized caller can enumerate these capsules without knowing a workflow ID; optional tracking is never required. A capsule with an incomplete transfer includes its complete retained transfer proposal and original locally accepted phase inputs. workflow.get and workflow.list expose them under current receiving authorization so recovery never depends on the original client or an optional report. The complete immutable proposal and its canonical digest survive original-client loss; its type, workflow ID and complete child-request/Plan closure match this capsule. advances retains authority-discriminated driver advance, owner-native final settlement and owner-native lifecycle decision inputs with their finite outcomes. Every retained lifecycle decision must match its exact predecessor and the current capsule state; terminal history can never be relabeled as live work. Transfer completion is performed only through workflow.advance with the full commit closure; it preserves the installed procedure phase and lifecycle state atomically with transfer completion. A separate normally authorized driver advance owns subsequent procedure progress. Independently authorized owner-native settlement may record the final completed facts of already admitted work while preserving incomplete transfer custody; it does not admit new work or complete that transfer. bindings retains complete later-reviewed child Plans, authenticated predecessor/material lineage and original binding requests without changing the immutable proposal. Unbound continuation slots cannot authorize child work or be skipped when completing their installed phase. Driver-transfer progress is orthogonal to lifecycle state. Freeze and commit preserve prepared, active, paused or recovery-required status; completion changes only transfer custody and driver authority. Terminal capsules reject new transfers, while exact previously accepted transfer requests remain replayable. Recovery custody is present only on a newly identified successor prepared through workflow.recover; incomplete recovery preparation forbids child admission, binding, phase advance and transfer. Its committed lineage never retargets original records or reexecutes completed child slots. An initial capsule always retains its exact local PreparationWitness in prerequisite_witnesses. Before first ordinary phase progress or child admission the owner independently authenticates and retains the complete same-proposal participant preparation closure. Merely preparing a local capsule, supplying matching IDs or transferring the driver does not waive this agreement. Committed recovery preparation supplies the corresponding agreement for successor capsules. Every ordinary phase transition preserves complete original phase evidence and ordered accepted history; neither evidence nor intermediate transitions can be erased from a later capsule. states.json owns the lifecycle meanings and edges. Paused capsules block new child admission, binding and ordinary phase progress until an independently authorized native resume reconciles current driver, accepted child and hold facts. Same-phase transfer completion and final native settlement of already admitted work may preserve or finish paused custody. Cancelled capsules permanently close local future child admission while preserving accepted child outcomes, exact replay, complete proposal/input/hold custody and pending transfer evidence. Initial local cancellation does not require a complete participant preparation closure and never certifies that other participants stopped. It does not replace positive retirement at a participant that never prepared. Retained recovery successors must also prove admission order: every binding, advance, native lifecycle decision and local transfer phase uses an original expected_generation at or after the committed recovery-preparation generation. A later committed marker cannot retroactively authorize changes accepted before that boundary. Explicit unused-successor abandonment remains the only pre-commit lifecycle path.

Hold.description: An owner-enforced restriction protecting a resource while accepted work or unresolved effects retain custody. Only its release condition and owner evidence permit release; elapsed time or a cancellation request does not establish that condition.

consistency_scope.description: Application-quiesced asserts one verified writer fence/cohort covering every captured preserved dataset. Independent-datasets provides only individually consistent recovery points and must not be advertised as application-atomic.

quiescence_evidence.description: Exact durable independent owner evidence establishing one common write-quiescence interval and capture generation across all preserved datasets, or null when no application-wide consistency is claimed. A digest is not itself proof of native fencing.

Checkpoint.description: A complete checkpoint binds every required captured dataset, accepted release and secret generations, independent signed native capture receipts and verified backup snapshot identity. Its witness subject covers the entire canonical checkpoint body excluding the witness, including consistency_scope and quiescence_evidence. Application-quiesced requires one verifiable writer fence and capture cohort; independent-datasets is explicitly not an application-atomic recovery point. No missing dataset or inconsistent archive may be silently omitted.

Release.description: An immutable closure of the exact software, settings, bindings, secret receipts and recovery inputs selected for one application instance. A release existing in source or storage does not prove owner admission or current activation.

evidence.description: The complete evidence selection: at most 64 digests inline, or an exact ProblemEvidence RecordReference for the whole selection. The inline threshold bounds representation, not total evidence. A reference requires a non-null Problem owner and resource matching its protected owner/resource identity. Every read separately reauthorizes that disclosure scope; failure reporting grants no bearer access. Never silently drop evidence or divide one selection into unrelated errors to fit a frame.

Problem.description: An actionable account of what is known and the permitted next step for the named owner/resource. Preserve uncertainty and exact request identity; a failure summary must not imply that earlier effects were undone.

SourceProposal.description: Reviewable changes to source against an exact base. changes is complete for the requested capture scope; an empty list records a completed capture with no differences from that base in that scope. tree_digest still identifies the exact resulting captured tree. Missing or incomplete inspection cannot be reported as an empty successful capture. The proposal preserves live edits for review; it is distinct from publication, accepted configuration and activated application state.

Grant.description: A scoped commitment made by the local host owner to an application. Application source may refer to an approved grant but cannot grant itself new host authority.

Binding.description: An explicit connection between a provider interface and its consumer, with exact generation and compatibility evidence. Naming a dependency alone does not prove this connection is active.

Fence.description: Evidence that the previous writer has been prevented from writing in the named scope. Loss of contact, DNS withdrawal or removal of a caller credential alone is not such evidence.

history_complete.description: False explicitly reports that terminal history has been pruned. Active, uncertain and recovery-required work must remain discoverable. Neither page exhaustion nor historical absence proves no earlier effect. Terminal detail collection never frees accepted request identities. The original owner epoch retains exact replay and changed-payload rejection independently of this listing; capacity exhaustion refuses new identities instead of reusing accepted ones.

OperationPage.description: A bounded complete page of the permission-filtered owner traversal, with a type discriminator even when empty. Continuations retain the same owner epoch, authenticated principal, resource filter and active/history selection; concurrent changes must not silently omit retained entries. A non-null cursor requires continuation before claiming the traversal is complete. A single large record is delivered as its exact RecordReference; page bounds do not require dropping, truncating or splitting its logical contents. Inline records and references identify the same owner and unique record identities. Each reference must be completely retrieved before claiming its record has been inspected.

history_complete.description: False explicitly reports that terminal history has been pruned. Active, uncertain and recovery-required work must remain discoverable. Neither page exhaustion nor historical absence proves no earlier effect.

WorkflowPage.description: A bounded complete page of the permission-filtered owner traversal, with a type discriminator even when empty. Continuations retain the same owner epoch, authenticated principal, resource filter and active/history selection; concurrent changes must not silently omit retained entries. A non-null cursor requires continuation before claiming the traversal is complete. A single large record is delivered as its exact RecordReference; page bounds do not require dropping, truncating or splitting its logical contents. Inline records and references identify the same owner and unique record identities. Each reference must be completely retrieved before claiming its record has been inspected.

ObservationPage.description: A bounded complete page of one permission-filtered owner observation traversal, retaining the owner epoch even when empty. Each inline observation and exact Observation RecordReference names that same owner and one distinct resource within the independently retained request selection. References pin their resource before disclosure and their complete payload must be verified before claiming inspection. Continuations retain the authenticated principal, exact selection and owner epoch; concurrent changes must not silently omit retained entries. A non-null cursor requires continuation before claiming the traversal is complete. A single large observation uses its exact immutable reference, never truncated evidence or a new total collection limit. Page and snapshot owner identify the attributed observation owner, not an intermediary transport or cache. Cached and caller-reported observations preserve their declared origin, owner epoch and original time; snapshotting never relabels them as fresh evidence. Current custody of prior epochs uses the separate history protocol rather than rewriting original ownership.

EventPage.description: A complete bounded page of the exact owner-epoch/resource log traversal, even when events is empty. The opaque continuation binds the authenticated principal, exact query, retained traversal and owner epoch. Every resumed request supplies that owner and resource; an epoch change, expired cursor or changed query rejects and requires an explicit restart. A null next_cursor exhausts this retained traversal; a non-null cursor requires continuation regardless of page length. Concurrent appends and owner restoration cannot silently reuse an integer offset or omit retained entries. gap explicitly reports missing retained history and is preserved across the traversal; log absence is never proof that an effect did not occur. Event cursor integers are ordered positions within this pinned traversal, not reusable continuation tokens.

expires_at.description: Owner-chosen deadline for creating a new plan or admitting a new reference, checked against the owner clock without waiting for collection. Existing accepted work retains its original inputs and replay semantics after this deadline. Null means no admission deadline.

ContentStaging.description: Durable pre-admission input custody, not accepted execution. content.begin replays the same caller-allocated staging ID only for the same owner epoch, actual principal, resource, purpose, digest and size; changed input conflicts. Uploading has no immutable handle and accepts only complete bounded chunks at an exact offset; repeated bytes at that offset are idempotent, conflicting bytes fail. Commit verifies all declared bytes and digest before exposing an immutable staging-bound handle. All later reads, status and retries reauthorize the actual principal against protected custody. Expiry applies only without accepted references and never authorizes collection of accepted input. A missing/restored owner or expired identity cannot be treated as permission to recreate it silently. A committed handle past its admission deadline may remain retained by earlier accepted work, but cannot authorize a new plan or request. Accepted replay is resolved before new-input expiry checks. workflow-input custody uses the exact workflow resource identity and is pinned by accepted preparation, advance or transfer, including before child operations exist. Size is limited only by the interoperable integer range and independently approved receiver capacity; collection, participant and evidence counts are not transport limits.

WorkflowTransferProposal.description: The immutable transfer preimage shared by all receiving owners: exact workflow and transfer identities, original driver principal/term, next driver principal and complete participant owner/resource closure. The next term is expected_term plus one. The receiving owner independently compares this proposal to its protected capsule and current authorization; the proposal grants no permission. Closure members are unique and the complete closure must match the retained workflow. Every freeze and commit witness binds digest(canonical JSON of this proposal), the workflow ID and its exact participant owner epoch. One owner witness covers all of that owner's resources in the proposal; a resource outside the closure cannot be admitted by it. workflow_proposal_digest equals every receiver capsule immutable proposal_digest; it commits the complete installed procedure, target and child Plan/input closure in every freeze and commit attestation. Matching workflow IDs and resource closures cannot substitute for this exact intent agreement.

WorkflowTransferRequest.description: A phase request for one receiving owner. New requests compare the exact local capsule generation and independently verify current driver and resource authority. The owner resolves the retained transfer ID and phase before freshness checks: an identical durably accepted phase request returns its retained outcome despite a later capsule generation, while any changed preimage conflicts and never creates another transfer. Freeze blocks old-driver admission atomically with durable transfer custody; commit requires independently authenticated freeze witnesses for every distinct participant owner and cannot infer them from timeout or absent work. The receiving owner's supplied freeze witness must exactly match its retained local freeze. These are owner obligations, not a native coordinator implementation. A durably accepted local freeze atomically retains its frozen witness with the original phase input; a lost response must leave both discoverable.

WorkflowTransferPhase.description: The exact original phase input retained by this receiving owner. Reconstruct its WorkflowTransferRequest using the enclosing capsule owner and retained proposal. The original expected_generation and supplied witness records survive newer generations so another authorized caller can retry exactly without client files.

WorkflowTransfer.description: Discoverable transfer custody retained in every receiving Workflow. accepted_phases preserves each locally accepted input; freeze_witnesses and commit_witnesses retain independently verified evidence with states frozen and transferred respectively. Missing evidence remains missing. Freeze retains the original driver; commit records this owner's durable new term only after the complete freeze closure; completed additionally requires every participant-owner commit witness. A partial transfer remains incomplete in this orthogonal transfer record and cannot silently restore old admission or authorize a different transfer. An owner keeps exact replay results in protected history even after this field records a later transfer. Restored epochs require explicit recovery rather than inventing or retargeting the original transfer. Freeze phase includes this receiving owner's frozen witness; an input accepted without its retrievable local prerequisite is not a completed freeze. Transfer witnesses use the same proposal digest and exact owner epoch, and their generation identifies the local durable phase commit; later capsule changes preserve them. Each local phase witness generation is greater than its original expected_generation and no greater than the current capsule generation; the local freeze witness generation is no greater than the original commit expected_generation. Lifecycle state is never overwritten by transfer progress. Paused and recovery-required restrictions survive completion; transfer is not a recovery action. The new driver delivers the complete transferred-witness closure through workflow.advance.transfer_completion. That advance atomically marks this transfer completed and retains its immutable AdvanceReceipt; exact accepted replay cannot repeat the transition. Lifecycle changes do not erase accepted freeze or commit custody: a later cancelled or completed capsule retains that incomplete evidence for inspection and exact accepted replay, without permission for a new phase. Completion preserves the current procedure phase; it cannot be combined with resumption or ordinary phase progress. Retained local freeze and commit witness generations are interleaved with workflow lifecycle history. A new local transfer phase cannot follow terminal completion, cancellation or recovery-successor abandonment, even if a later capsule merely claims that phase was already accepted. Every earlier accepted phase remains retained and replayable after terminal lifecycle changes. Retained new binding generations must also lie outside the closed driver-admission interval from local freeze through separate transfer completion; a later capsule cannot fabricate a binding that bypassed the same restriction enforced on live admission.

WorkflowTransferWitness.description: A signed finite local freeze or commit attestation. The complete proposal digest binds the workflow, original and next drivers and every participant owner/resource. Together with this exact owner epoch, local capsule generation and frozen/transferred state, it supplies the transfer prerequisite. evidence_digests is empty because further recovery evidence is retained separately in the workflow, not in this bounded attestation. Native receivers independently authenticate the witness and verify the full proposal closure before changing admission or driver authority.

ProblemEvidence.description: The complete immutable evidence digest selection of a Problem for one exact owner epoch and resource. The owner establishes durable retrievable custody before publishing its RecordReference, without admitting an operation. Complete size, digest, installed schema and owner/resource identity must verify before the selection is used. Each snapshot read independently authorizes the current receiving principal against protected disclosure scope. A rejection need not disclose private evidence, but any advertised selection is complete and retained for its advertised traversal. Evidence extent has no transport count limit; independently approved receiver capacity may explicitly reject new custody, never silently truncate it.
